shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large upright stone slab/pillar
horizontal register bands dividing the composition
row of repeated small motifs along a band
rectangular framed glyph-like or block-like signs
justification: Both are low-relief carvings on upright slabs organised into horizontal registers, with animal figures in profile and rows of repeated small units along a band, which gives a loose compositional echo. But the specific content differs entirely: A shows an elaborate anthropomorphic figure with headdress plumes and columns of square glyph blocks in a dense, curvilinear, layered style, while B shows isolated, boldly outlined, schematic zoomorphs (quadrupeds, a long-necked bird, a fox-like beast) set against an empty ground with no glyphic or human elements.
